question: How do independent cell-cycle timing, transmitted types and common calendar rates affect the specificity of family-selected horizon contrasts, and what additional discrimination is supplied by prospectively eligible sister-subtree survival?
scope: Hypothetical dimensionless branching models, no empirical fit, target discovery or first-ever novelty claim. Quantify a known possibility, not rediscover age dependence or generic lineage covariance.
known_before_freeze: Published homogeneous/shared-calendar invariance and earlier source/finite-record audits.
Deterministic-age first-generation counterexample derived informally before this study; its formula depends on selection horizon.
Established Erlang competing-risk and lineage-correlation literature; Iyer already includes age-dependent baseline models.
Close prior art for paired sister-subtree statistics located in Korsnes 2023; exact binary/fixed-lag and horizon-statistic pairing not established novel.

No numerical Q, horizon-contrast, sister-covariance or early-time-loss outcomes from this grid have been generated. Analytic resource bounds and the no-division low-count probability were evaluated for planning.
A first-event small-time expansion was derived and independently checked symbolically before any new outcomes; related Erlang-plus-exponential leading powers have established prior art.
The original unfrozen 60+12 model grid is retained; deterministic primary computation replaces the unfrozen bootstrap proposal, with full-grid complete-tree Monte Carlo validation.

estimands.founder: Prospective fixed newborn or specified initial-stage founder; every extinct and never-dividing family retained.
estimands.tag: Fair future-blind daughter choice at each division; equivalently integrate 2^(-generation) weights across living descendants.
estimands.family: F_T=1 if any descendant alive at T.
estimands.Q: E[F_T U(t)]/P(F_T), with t<=T; no ratio if denominator is zero.
estimands.contrast: Q_later(t)-Q_earlier(t), same absolute early t and founder law.
estimands.pair: At most one pair per founder: both daughters of its first division if that event occurs by2 before death. Follow each subtree for equal fixed lag; no future-survival or completeness selection.
estimands.covariance: Cov(A1(s),A2(s)|eligible first division), where Aj=1 if any descendant of daughter j is alive at lag s.
estimands.calendar_residual: Pooled mean E[(A1-h(b,b+s))*(A2-h(b,b+s)) | eligible], where b varies over qualifying first-division birth times and the known calendar-model h is conditioned on each b. This is not a covariance after sample recentering.

validation_only_times.purpose: U(T), Q_T(T), family survival and time-zero identities; endpoint queries are not additional primary contrast times.
validation_only_times.deterministic_extras: Both deterministic primary and MC evaluate t1.25 underT1.5 and1.75; retain U/F at union0,.5,1,1.25,1.5,1.75,2,3,4.

model_rules.time_units: Dimensionless; no mapping to doses or real cancer-cell cycle durations.
model_rules.potential_division: Erlang(k, rate=k/mean_z), competing with an independent exponential death clock of rate mu.
model_rules.type_kernel: Each daughter independently copies mother type with probability rho, otherwise redraws an independent fair type. K_zv=rho*1[z=v]+(1-rho)/2. Initial type probability 1/2.
model_rules.initial_stage: newborn=stage1; uniform_stage=uniform over1..k with the remaining exponential stages. This is not a stable population age distribution. Every daughter starts stage1.
model_rules.calendar: lambda(b)=1+0.5*sin(pi*b), shared absolute calendar time, constant mu.
model_rules.deterministic: Potential division at age1 for every cell; competing independent exponential death.
model_rules.same_mean_limit: Type constructions share initial potential-timer mixture only; observed competing-risk marginals and growth need not match.
model_rules.event_boundary: Alive on [birth,event); a division at a query time replaces parent with both daughters at that time.

primary_method.method: Finite-state backward branching survival ODE plus positive marked joint ODE for Erlang/type models; exact scalar recursion for deterministic-age; quadrature/known identities for calendar and no-division controls.
primary_method.solver: SciPy solve_ivp DOP853, rtol1e-10, atol1e-12; convergence rerun at rtol1e-12, atol1e-14.
primary_method.numerical_gates: Absolute probability/contrast difference <=1e-8 between formulations/tolerances. Do not clip nontrivial discrepancies or choose successful cases. Record full maximum errors.
primary_method.qualifying_weights: Mother-type weights proportional to initial type/stage mixture times integral_0^2 exp(-mu*b)*residual-ErlangPDF(b)db. Use qualifying weights, not initial1/2.
primary_method.pair_identity: For two types, C(s)=rho^2*w0*w1*(h_01(s)-h_11(s))^2 under independent daughters conditional on mother. Single-type and rho0 have zero covariance.
primary_method.calendar_raw: Integrate h(b,b+s) and its square over qualifying first-division density lambda(b)*exp(-integral_0^b lambda-mu*b). Raw covariance is variance across birth times; correctly residualized cross-product has expectation0.

independent_verification.deterministic: Separate forward marked/extinction calculation with independent implementation; every case retained. Closed-form and recursive controls checked independently.

monte_carlo.rng: One sequential NumPy Generator PCG64 per case, SeedSequence([2026111012,seed_case_index]); ascending batches of250, stable breadth-first arrays. No promise of batch-size or version invariance.
monte_carlo.resource_guard: Stop affected case before allocation if total generated-cell count including founders/newborns at4 would exceed50,000,000, or a proposed frontier would exceed5,000,000cells. Preserve completed batches, RNG state, diagnostics and incomplete status. Never cap/omit/redraw a family. Catch resource failures explicitly; do not label prefix as completed10000founder case.
monte_carlo.observations: Store per-founder U values, family indicators and eligible sister-pair outcomes locally for reproducibility; publish aggregate results plus seed/code hashes.
monte_carlo.precision: Record selection and eligible-pair counts; counts below100 are flagged low precision and retained. Undefined denominators are not zero.
monte_carlo.comparisons: Probability diagnostics use the331 predeclared gates. Q/contrast/U/covariance/residual diagnostics record estimates, model expectations, founder or pair MCSE and flags above6*SE+1e-8 when precision contracts are met. These are numerical consistency diagnostics, not biological hypothesis tests. Every unresolved/flagged result remains visible.
monte_carlo.interpretation: These comparisons assess numerical simulation consistency, not biological hypothesis significance. No bootstrap needed for exact deterministic primary values; initial unfrozen proposal bootstrap was replaced before outcomes.
monte_carlo.failures: Investigate and retain every mismatch; fixes/versioning cannot alter scientific grid to favor results.
draw_order: Initial fair types, then uniform founder stages where applicable.
For each stable active array: potential division timers, then independent death timers; mu0 has infinite death time without drawing.

Successful divisions preserve parent order; daughters interleaved child0,child1. For two types, one uniform per daughter gives stay probability(1+rho)/2, including rho0/rho1; every daughter starts stage1.
Draw unused clocks consistently even for cells born exactly at the administrative endpoint; their live-at-birth contribution is retained.

Calendar potential division uses an Exp(1) hazard increment and vectorized bisection of integrated lambda on[birth,4] to absolute time tolerance1e-12; increments exceeding remaining hazard imply no division within support.
monte_carlo.boundaries: Alive on[birth,event); divisions exactly at queries replace parent with both daughters including births at4. Synthetic division/death ties choose death. Nonpositive computed lifetimes, underflowed positive chronological weights, or unsupported topology are explicit failures.

estimators.contrast: Difference of Q estimates, with SE from the paired difference of their founder influence arrays.
estimators.unconditional_U: Mean U across all10000 roots, SE=sample_sd(U,ddof1)/sqrt(N).
estimators.covariance: For M>=2 eligible pairs, M/(M-1)*(mean(A1*A2)-mean(A1)*mean(A2)); SE=M/(M-1)*sample_sd((A1-Abar)*(A2-Bbar)-C_plugin,ddof1)/sqrt(M). Undefined for fewer than2 pairs.
estimators.calendar_residual: Mean R=(A1-h(b,b+s))*(A2-h(b,b+s)) over eligible pairs, SE=sample_sd(R,ddof1)/sqrt(M); independent known-model survival quadrature.
estimators.precision: Approximate SE diagnostics require each relevant selected/pair count>=100. Zero-SE nontrivial comparisons are unresolved precision checks, not success; structural exact constants can be checked directly.

probability_checks.test: Exact two-sided binomial with model probability; conditional mother-type0 counts use M eligible pairs and model w0. Flag p<0.001/331; no independence assumption required for Bonferroni. Undefined M0 mother-type checks retained. p0/p1 require exact logical behavior.

monte_carlo.near_zero_scope: Near-zero loss checks are deterministic only. The finite Monte Carlo cohort is not used to resolve events far below its sampling resolution.
monte_carlo.pre_execution: Complete implementation and independent code/fixture review before full scientific outcomes. Record final code hash and source/protocol pins; preserve explicit failures.

controls: Homogeneous k1 selected curve matches the published finite-horizon formula at all horizons; duplicate k1 initializations retained.
No-division and zero-death Q=1 whenever defined; no-division pair estimand undefined.
Common calendar-rate model obeys horizon invariance; raw pair covariance may arise from pooling birth times, residual expected cross-product=0.
For all constant-death models E[U(t)]=exp(-mu*t), and Q_T(T)*P(F_T)=E[U(T)]. This is not an inheritance diagnostic.
Prospective independent-renewal sisters have covariance0; persistent-type covariance formula and correct qualifying weights.
Permanent shared family environment with the same fixed type-specific rates is observationally equivalent to rho1 inherited type; no universal inheritance claim.

reporting.all_grid: Publish every case, all12primary contrasts/case, all3pair lags and all controls, negative/zero/opposite results included.
reporting.no_outcome_selection: No favored time, phenotype, initialization or threshold chosen after results. Descriptive maxima across the declared grid are labeled as such, not significance-selected findings.
reporting.claims: Paired statistics can distinguish these stipulated alternatives only within assumptions. Positive covariance does not uniquely establish inheritance. Prior studies are not refuted by this abstract calculation.
reporting.revision: Freeze after independent design review and before any new numerical outcome. Scientific amendments get separate records; implementation fixes preserve failed first runs and exact changes.

early_time_prediction.status: Symbolic candidate derived before freeze, no new numerical outcomes inspected.
early_time_prediction.fixed_horizon: T in2,3,4 held strictly positive whilet tends to0; death mu>0 and positive finite division rates.
early_time_prediction.newborn_formula: For common Erlang shape k, coefficient A_T=mu*sum_z p_z*alpha_z^k*(K h_newborn(T))_z / ((k+1)!*H_initial(T)); 1-Q_T(t)=A_T*t^(k+1)+O(t^(k+2)). Initial p is fair for2types.
early_time_prediction.cancellation: Homogeneous iid newborn renewal gives A=mu*alpha^k/(k+1)!, independentT. At rho0, initial p equals the fair daughter redraw law, yielding A=mu*mean_z(alpha_z^k)/(k+1)! independentT. Arbitrary initial type laws need not cancel.
early_time_prediction.uniform_stage_formula: Leading order becomes2 with A_T=mu*sum_z[p_z*(alpha_z/k)*(K h_newborn(T))_z]/(2*H_initial(T)), generally horizon dependent even without inherited type. This is quadratic, not linear death onset.
early_time_prediction.zero_death: Q=1; positive leading-term ratio undefined, not zero-imputed.
early_time_prediction.numeric_grid: All63 Erlang cases and everyT2,3,4; t=epsilon/max(alpha_z), epsilon=.01,.001,.0001. No Monte Carlo near-zero estimate promised: these events can be far below achievable sample resolution.
early_time_prediction.method: Positive tagged-death/family-survival ODE rescaled by stage-specific powers of t; avoid subtracting Q from1. Validate against positive-J complements at ordinary primary evaluation times and independent checks.
early_time_prediction.comparison: Publish every ratio (1-Q)/(A_T*t^power) for mu>0. At smallest epsilon, predeclared numerical-asymptotic diagnostic absolute relative discrepancy<=0.01; this is not a proved uniform remainder bound or statistical threshold. Retain failures, all earlier epsilon ratios and tighter-solver discrepancies.
early_time_prediction.interpretation: Apparent early multistep order can reflect founder age and family selection; it is not a biochemical mechanism, globally equivalent lifetime law, clinically measurable predictor, or first-ever theorem claim.
early_time_prediction.proven_grid_envelope: For mu>0, fixedT and the stated initialization/kernel, a first-sister lower bound and all-discarded-sisters union upper bound give exp(-3*epsilon)<=R<=exp(6*epsilon) on this grid, where R=(1-Q)/(positive leading term). Conservative constants; no monotonic error claim. The finite-epsilon envelope is checked with numerical slack1e-7; the .01 smallest-epsilon diagnostic is retained.
